# Project Falcon: Team Charter

**Team:** Project Falcon · **Owner:** Engineering Manager, Falcon · **Updated:** 12 October 2026

Project Falcon is the rebuild of the **KestrelTrack Driver app**, the mobile app that delivery drivers use to get routes, scan parcels and capture proof of delivery. Our launch customer is **Bharat Freight**, who will move 4,000 drivers to the new app.

## 1. Why we're doing this

Out of scope for this release: route optimisation changes, the customer-facing tracking page, iOS tablets.

## 5. The mobile release train

- The Driver app ships on a **release train every second Wednesday**.
- The release branch is cut on the **Monday before** release at 10:00.
- **QA sign-off must be given at least 24 hours before** the release, so by Tuesday 10:00.
- Store submission is done by the Engineering Manager after sign-off.

QA may sign off a release only when **all** of these are true:

1. **Zero open P1 and zero open P2 bugs** in the release.

3. The full regression suite passed on the release build within the last 24 hours.
4. Smoke tests passed on at least one real Android and one real iOS device.
5. Release notes are reviewed.

A strike is a formal, recorded warning given in Trellis by a manager who has permission to give strikes (normally the Engineering Manager). The person receives it in their Trellis inbox along with the reason.

| Missing an agreed deadline without telling anyone beforehand | Telling your lead early is never a strike |
| Three unexcused absences in a calendar month | See section 3 |
| Sharing Confidential or Restricted data outside Kestrel | Serious cases go straight to the HR Manager |
| Deploying to production outside the deploy rules without approval | See the Engineering Handbook |
| Not reporting a lost laptop or phone within the required time | See the Information Security Policy |
